quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under ride in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge right and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Increasing your speed is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride on water and lose grip. This is called hydroplaning. Lower your speed on wet roads to avoid losing control.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You can turn right after slowing down and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You can turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
If pedestrians are crossing.
If you are turning right.
If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but a vehicle is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right because of road construction.
The road ahead turns sharply at a very steep angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at a very steep angle.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns drivers to slow down and prepare for a sharp turn.

questions.question: If you keep a valid license for one full year without getting any moving violations, you may earn a Good Point on your driving record.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: If you keep a valid license for one full year without getting any moving violations, you may earn a Good Point on your driving record.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to say they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you must let that vehicle go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Other drivers may not see you.
Vehicles behind you might follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights in fog or mist. The light will bounce back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help you drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce how much you can see at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles. This makes your pupils shrink. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that tells drivers about traffic laws. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn about danger. This sign warns about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires float on water instead of gripping the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning when it rains?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive slower.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: When it rains, drive slower to reduce the chance of hydroplaning. Driving too fast can make your tires float on water and lose grip with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always give emergency vehicles the right-of-way when you see flashing lights or hear a siren.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a highway from a ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when there is space.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed. Let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low overpass ahead. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.
